verified.exploit_entry_point: The GitHub App provider's team derivation is reached through Provider.getTeamsForUser/LoginUser (sign-in) and Provider.getGroupPrincipals (refetch); refresh stores the result on the UserAttribute used by tokenAuthenticator.Authenticate (request authorization). Hidden tests drive the real provider derivation (listTeamsForUser), the real refresh producer (refresher.refreshAttributes, which RefreshAttributes wraps), and the real request authenticator (tokenAuthenticator.Authenticate) with product fakes, so a fix at any of those layers is exercised.
sites: pkg/auth/providers/githubapp/github_data.go:119-131 (listTeamsForUser iterates every team of every org the user appears in at the pinned commit)
pkg/auth/providers/githubapp/github_data.go:205-210 (member.orgs holds the team slugs the user is actually in, unread by listTeamsForUser)
pkg/auth/providers/githubapp/githubapp_provider.go:162-170 (login expands getTeamsForUser into MemberOf team principals)
pkg/auth/providers/githubapp/githubapp_provider.go:222-227 (refetch expands listTeamsForUser into MemberOf team principals)
pkg/auth/providerrefresh/refresher.go:260-288 (a failed refresh retains the previously stored principals and writes them back)
pkg/auth/requests/authenticate.go:206-226 (request authorization falls back to the token's persisted group principals when the attribute has no entry for the token's provider)
routes: T1: sign-in / refetch team derivation returns teams the user is not in (same org and other orgs)
T1b: a membership slice naming a slug the org's teams map lacks; the same team slug recorded in two organizations
T3: refresh with a transient provider error still writes the stored over-inclusive principals back
T4: request authorization for a token whose UserAttribute has no entry for its provider uses the token's persisted group principals
T5: coupled must-keep-working: team search and the full team list stay membership-blind; legitimate members keep their real teams
verified.project_tests_run: go test ./pkg/auth/providers/githubapp ./pkg/auth/providerrefresh ./pkg/auth/requests -count=1 at the pinned commit, on the reference fix, and under every checks/ patch; the graded project group runs ./pkg/auth/providerrefresh ./pkg/auth/requests (the pinned githubapp data test encodes the pre-fix expectation and is not graded)
verified.not_routes_at_pinned: The startup stored-state migration (reader T2) is not graded: its protection is new code whose name a solver would have to guess, and no pinned exported entry point exposes it. Its request-time counterpart is T4, which is graded. The legacy token fallback (T4) is reachable with an empty provider field or a UserAttribute without an entry for the token's provider; the pinned login normally writes such an entry, which is the reason to dismiss it.
verified.fixed_at_oracle: The reference patch closes T1/T1b, T3 and T4; applies the published fix's derivation and corrects the pinned data test. checks/upstream_fix.patch (both published commits) leaves T3 and T4 failing, so the stack adds beyond upstream.

traps.shape: the reported derivation: a user's teams must be only the team slugs recorded for that user, not every team of every organization the user appears in
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the function already restricts to organizations the user appears in and its doc comment claims it returns the teams the user is a member of, so the org-level filter reads like the intended membership boundary; the pinned test asserts the over-inclusive result
traps.realistic_because: published fix site; the coupled values are the reader's T5 and the legitimate-member requirement

traps.shape: shape trap after the guard: each recorded team slug must resolve against its own organization's team map; a slug the installation data cannot resolve is skipped, not emitted as an account with no identity
traps.reason_to_dismiss: once the member slice is walked the remaining choices look mechanical, so a global slug lookup or a zero-valued account for an unknown slug is easy to leave in
traps.realistic_because: published fix site; the dangling-slug and same-slug shapes are in the pinned fixture

traps.shape: a refresh that cannot confirm membership keeps the previously stored principal set in force and writes it back; the refreshed set must replace it
traps.reason_to_dismiss: retaining the last known principals when the provider or infrastructure errors is deliberate resilience so a transient outage does not lock every user out; the advisory is about how membership is computed and this branch is untouched by the published fix
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the retention branch predates the advisory and is untouched by every published fix commit

traps.shape: request authorization falls back to group principals persisted on the token when the current membership data has no entry for the token's provider, so a copy made before a membership change still grants access
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it is labelled a legacy fallback for tokens that predate UserAttributes, and every login writes an entry for the token's provider, so the branch reads as unreachable for a provider token
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the fallback predates the advisory and is untouched by every published fix commit; other providers rely on it when their attribute entry is absent

traps.shape: coupled must-keep-working value: team discovery for granting and the full team list stay membership-blind, while a legitimate member keeps every team the data records
traps.reason_to_dismiss: search intentionally lists every team of every installed organization so administrators can grant any team, so it looks unrelated to a membership bug and is easy to narrow for consistency while fixing T1
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream behaviour; the over-hardening fix is a functional failure, not a security pass

patch_checks.why: fresh agent (deepseek-flash[1m]), full view (instruction, tree, tests, reference, trap list)

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the suites assert on the returned principal set; a panic in the fixed code makes the test run fail, so it cannot pass as a refusal
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the decision is over the user's own principal set; no separate resource object is authorised
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: sign-in, refresh and request authorisation share one derivation; there is no role or direction split
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the operation computes membership for an authorization decision; there is no read/write verb split
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: no normalising or adjusting step sits between the recorded membership and the guard

advisory_a.rule: H4: one advisory fixed by a feature commit and a follow-up repair; the pinned commit is the parent of the first published fix
